_comment: Least-privilege IAM policy for LIVE sending (P5). DO NOT ATTACH until the
sending domain is verified in SES, its DNS is confirmed, and a dry run has
completed cleanly. Until then keep docs/ses-iam-policy.json attached, which
It adds exactly one permission to the P3 policy: ses:SendEmail, and only
- for the one verified sending domain identity,
- through the one configuration set (without which SES emits no events),
- from an address on that domain (ses:FromAddress condition).
Raw, bulk and templated sends stay denied: the application uses Simple
content only, so a credential that can do more is a credential whose leak
can do more. Identity deletion stays denied for the reasons in the P3 policy.
This policy governs OUTBOUND mail only. It grants nothing related to
receiving, and inbound mail for the domain stays with the existing provider
and its MX records, which this application never reads or changes.
